name: Stoïk
description: European cyber-risk company combining cyber insurance with cybersecurity services — prevent, detect, recover. Sold primarily through insurance brokers. Founded Oct 2021, France. ~2,000 estimated users.

mentions.evidence: MRR $0 / 0 seat subscriptions (premium / service txn), ~$40,146 L30, ~$23,282,016 all-time. Last sync Oct 4, 2026 ~08:14 Warsaw (06:14 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Pair a licensed niche (cyber, professional indemnity, contractors' liability) with productized security / ops tooling sold via brokers. Compliance is the moat; software is the leverage.

whyItPrints: Regulated insurance + security hybrid. Premiums and services invoice through Stripe without classic seat MRR ($0 MRR / 0 subs) but ~$40k L30 and a staggering ~$23.3M all-time. Conductor-lane energy: own a regulated risk workflow, charge when coverage renews.
whyThisMatters:
European brokers sell a cyber policy that includes the security work. The buyer is a small or mid-size company. The package is the insurance, the monitoring, and the response if an attack lands.

Prevention covers technical risk, staff habits, managed detection, and email. If something breaks, Stoïk's own engineers handle the incident and try to get the systems back up. They pay the claim, so they also run the watch. Brokers get a tool for explaining the risk and placing the cover. IT shops can add that round-the-clock monitoring to what they already sell. Partners get a NIS2 guide.

They say more than 14,000 European companies are covered, more than 150 incidents a month, and more than 2,000 brokers across seven markets. A broker can open a partner login and put the policy in front of clients. The company started in France in October 2021.
